speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: On 13 August, Saturday morning in Singapore, history was made.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: When Majulah Singapura was played for the first time at an Olympic Games, it was really quite an emotional experience for our President and all of us who were there.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: It was a moment of great national pride not just for Joseph and his family, but for our entire nation.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Singaporeans everywhere watching this moment on TV sang the anthem together with Joseph.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I believe for years to come, Singaporeans will remember this moment when the Singapore flag flew highest and our national anthem rang out on the Olympic stage.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: It has been far from an easy journey.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Joseph had to put in a tremendous amount of hard work and made many personal sacrifices.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: But this did not deter him at all.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: In fact, his father Colin Schooling remembered a time when he was woken up at 4.00 am by Joseph, for swimming practice.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: From a young age, Joseph already had the mindset of a champion.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: He had big dreams and the determination to make it happen.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: When Joseph was 14 years old, he left Singapore to train at the renowned Bolles School in the United States.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: It takes great courage, passion and determination to say, "Yes, I want to be an Olympian and I will do whatever it takes." That was exactly the kind of resolve we see in Joseph, who has put in hour after hour of training through the years and is now breaking record after record.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: It takes a village to raise an Olympic champion, they say.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Joseph's number one fans and supporters are undoubtedly his parents, Colin and May.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: They dedicated their lives to supporting Joseph's Olympic dream.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: They made huge sacrifices to provide the fullest support possible to help their son realise his dreams.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: They were with Joseph every step of the way; they always believed in him, and cheered him on at all his swim meets.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Colin, as well as Joseph's grand-uncle Lloyd Valberg, were our national sportsmen as well – in softball and athletics respectively.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: In fact, Mr Valberg was Singapore's first-ever Olympian and he inspired Joseph to pursue sporting excellence, while embracing the values of dedication, hard work, discipline and resilience.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We thank the Singapore Swimming Association and head coach Sergio Lopez, too, for all their efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: In the past 18 months, Sergio has been instrumental in grooming our top swimming talents, including Quah Zheng Wen, who entered the semi-finals for two events in Rio.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Sergio had also coached Joseph during his time at the Bolles School.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Joseph now trains under Eddie Reese at the University of Texas who joined Sergio on the coaching staff at Rio.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The support from Sport Singapore and the Singapore National Olympic Council, along with his scholarship in the University of Texas, has provided Joseph the best possible environment for Joseph to perform to his best.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I would also like to acknowledge the Ministry of Defence for deferring Joseph's National Service commitments, so that he could concentrate on doing well in Rio, which he did with flying colours.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: It was wonderful to see the entire nation rallying behind Joseph and our Olympians, and celebrating together as one Team Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: As Joseph put it, "This moment is not about me.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: It is for my country, my friends, my family and all those people who supported me and believed in me." We saw this at the Southeast Asian Games last year, when Joseph won nine Gold medals on home soil to deafening cheers from the stands.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The Rio Olympics may be nearly 16,000 kilometres away, but Singaporeans from all walks of life were there in spirit and offered numerous messages of support and encouragement to Joseph and to our many athletes who are competing there.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Last Friday morning, many students and working adults alike paused what they were doing just to catch Joseph compete in the semi-finals.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: And on Saturday morning, the whole of Singapore came to a standstill for a minute.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: All our eyes were glued to the TV screens.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We were all gripped by a sense of excitement, anticipation and, finally, pure ecstasy and national pride as our sporting hero touched home in record-breaking time.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Joseph's Olympic Gold medal marks a milestone in Singapore's sporting history, and also a new beginning.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: It adds to the Paralympics Gold medal won by Yip Pin Xiu in Beijing in 2008.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We must build on this success to strengthen our culture of sports and make Singapore a sporting nation.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Joseph is one amongst many athletes who have flown our flag over the years.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: They have all sought to bring honour and glory to our nation and to scale the highest peaks.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: This year, we have 25 Olympians and 12 Paralympians who are exceptional athletes and an inspiration to all of us.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The Olympics and Paralympics are the world's pinnacle sporting events.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: To qualify for the Games is already an immense achievement and they have all done Singapore very proud.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Next month, our Paralympians, including Pin Xiu, will be taking over the torch in Rio.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: These are individuals who have overcome the toughest challenges in life despite their disabilities and are aiming to go one step further to bring sporting glory to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: They are all champions in their own right.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: So, I would also like to congratulate all our Team Singapore athletes for their extraordinary feats.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I hope they will inspire a new generation of sporting talents who are unafraid to chase their dreams and to work hard to achieve their goals.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I hope and know that all Singaporeans will continue to give them our fullest support, especially for those who are still competing in Rio.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: I believe Joseph's win can inspire young Singaporeans to chase the rainbow and go after their dreams, even in areas apart from sports.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The journey may be difficult and will require hard work and sacrifice, but with hard work, grit and determination, we can achieve great things.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: For example, the media reported how the Anglo-Chinese School (ACS) family did a "live" screening of Joseph's swim for about 500 students and teachers.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: One of the Year 5 students, Ken Zhang, said later that Schooling's victory is an inspiration to everyone.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Our "never-say-die" attitude and our determination to persevere and succeed against tough odds.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: With the same grit and spirit, we can rally together as One Team Singapore to do extraordinary things for many, many more years to come.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To qualify for the Olympics is already an extraordinary achievement.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To win an Olympic Gold medal is the dream of every Olympian.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For many athletes and nations around the world, the dream remains a dream.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For Joseph and Singapore, the dream has become reality.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I was at the OCBC Aquatic Centre to witness this historic moment with the Singapore Swimming Association and the rest of the local swimming fraternity.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: There were cheers, ecstatic screams and hugs when Joseph won the race in record time.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: It was an amazing moment that I share with all Singaporeans and one that I will never forget.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: From a young age while swimming for ACS (Independent), Joseph was already breaking Schools and National age-group records.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: At 16, he was also the youngest ever to be crowned Sportsman of the Year, an accolade he would go on to win two more times.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: His achievement at the Rio Olympics is the culmination of years of hard work and unwavering support from his family and friends around him.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: So, congratulations once again to Joseph, as well as to Mr and Mrs Schooling!

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This morning, I was at the airport to receive Joseph with many other Singaporeans, and I could feel the sense of pride and joy of those around me as we welcomed home Singapore's first-ever Olympic Gold medallist.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The entire nation cheered him on while he was in Rio and now we will celebrate together as One Team Singapore.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This will allow even more Singaporeans to join in the celebrations to share Joseph's and Singapore's joy and triumph of winning the Olympic Gold medal.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Joseph's victory is another milestone in our nation's sporting journey.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Like Joseph said, this Gold medal proves that even as a small country, we can do extraordinary things.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We just need to believe in ourselves and work hard to chase our dreams.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: When Joseph first met Michael Phelps, he was a young star-struck teenager, hoping to one day compete alongside his idol.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I met most of them at a Team Singapore Send-Off Reception last week.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: They were in high spirits and all ready to fly our flag high.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I urge all Singaporeans to cheer them on with the same fervour and passion.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Joseph and his family are here, so I want to convey my heartfelt congratulations to them once again.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Joseph, I am sure your best years are still ahead of you.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: All the best for the 2020 Olympic Games.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: All of Singapore will be behind you and every Team Singapore athlete who flies the flag for us so proudly, as you have done.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It was our constituency's National Day dinner and many of the residents had already watched the 100-metre butterfly Olympic final earlier.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: But when we saw you again, Joseph, on the starting block, the crowd roared.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Singaporeans of all races – Chinese, Malay, Indian and Eurasian – were spurring you on in your race, your 100-metre butterfly Olympic final.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: We watched you fly down Lane 4, Singapore's flag on your swimming cap and all of us roared until you touched the wall.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It is an honour to have you here today in Parliament House with your parents, Mr and Mrs Schooling.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: But it was also how you embraced your victory that has moved many people, many Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: You spoke highly of Michael Phelps and shared that to race for others greater than yourself is deeply motivating.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Like several Members of this House, I played hockey competitively.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Before every match, the team understood what it meant to have the Singapore flag over our heart on our jerseys.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: We would try to overcome the butterflies in our stomach before going on the pitch.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Once on the pitch, our single focus was the scoreboard, always looking to ensure Singapore was up, trying our best.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: As I watched you "live" on your starting block, I thought to myself how completely composed you looked, how you were getting rid of those butterflies, how you had laser-like focus.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Then you leapt, engulfed with only your thoughts in the silence of the water, knowing what it means to carry that Singapore flag in your heart.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: What you said at your press conference is completely true – that people from small countries can do extraordinary things.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: When I was 15 years old, I played one of the toughest hockey matches of my life.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: At the end of it, I remember our coach shouting from the sidelines, "Well done, sons!

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Lift your heads up high!" Joseph, well done, son, you have lifted our heads up high!

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Behind what seemed to us as an effortless 50.39 seconds must have been a lifetime of discipline, training and sacrifice.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Joseph's parents have given him the security to enable him to pursue his dreams, supported his passion for the sport, and tirelessly fought for his cause.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: They did not take the easy course of asking him to abandon his passion and buckle down to the more conventional paths of success.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Without them, Joseph becoming an Olympic champion would not have been possible.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Singapore has experienced the unifying nature of sports in the early years of nation building and was again reminded of what it meant to support our sporting heroes flying our flag.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Singaporeans from all walks of life, of all ages, tuned in to watch the 100-metre butterfly final.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Even my neighbour, who hardly talks to me, asked me in the lift whether I caught the event on TV.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The imagination of Singaporeans was captured by the exploits of a third-generation Singaporean about to be a world-beater.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Many have slogged to be selected to don the national colours, simply for the love of the sport and the privilege of representing Singapore.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: We well up with pride watching our compatriots representing little Singapore compete with the world's best.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: We know you have put in so much just to get there.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: With this, I would like to ask the House to give their whole-hearted support for this Motion.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 2.20 pm.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended at 1.53 pm until 2.20 pm.
